prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) coordinates incidents, dispatch, jurisdictional coverage, shared records, surge and mutual aid; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location, gathers callback and clinical/access details, preserves original reports and separates facts/estimates; produces Caller Location Correction Slip, receives Bedside Arrival Receipt and verifies arrival time. Keep caller connected when feasible during alternate-channel crew contact. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) resolves uncertainty, records priority/rationale/response level, sends Pediatric Acuity Note, validates surge and approves/documents temporary overrides before use; flags calls needing immediate radio access and reviews suspected-duplicate audit memo. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/priorities, advises specialty care/destinations and may advise prioritization when communications constrain response; no dispatch authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages readiness/surge/coverage, reviews coverage before moves, approves material coverage-reducing exceptions, sends Mutual Aid Release Form, receives Coverage Gap Bulletin and decides staffing/deployment adjustments. Retains authority until named successor acknowledges or higher-level command takes effect; outgoing shift records incidents, failures, temporary channels and pending decisions; incoming shift verifies assignments and paths before accepting control. Paramedic Crew reports readiness/status, position, changes and hazards; stages until relocation/direct assignment confirmed, reassesses pediatric patients en route, reports material changes and follows local safety procedures, not entering uncertain areas without confirmed instructions. Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival/handover, last confirmed position and safe status after contact returns; reassignment only when dispatch confirms obligations permit. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network reachability, backups, assignments, priority/routes, Coverage Gap Bulletin and uses change card to record channel changes/effective times. Failed voice contact: use approved data channel if available; timestamp every attempt. CAD Console shows latest confirmed unit status, time and source; Ambulance Coordination Platform timestamps changes, queues updates through brief interruptions, flags reconciliation, and distinguishes accepted mutual-aid resources from local units. Coverage checks compare successful radio checks with planned intervals. North/South Gate Status Boards separately show access affecting radio/movement; South produces South Access Lane Notice. Crews acknowledge/repeat critical location, priority and destination; retry/correct failed or discrepant calls; handoff needs acknowledgment/dispatch confirmation. Degraded-radio mode prioritizes emergency traffic/common picture; announce outages, affected areas/restoration; fallback channels require acknowledgment/repetition before movement. Fleet Maintenance Cell promptly escalates radio

Document units:
S224: The Triage Supervisor reviews cases in which acuity decisions or escalation timing may have affected patient risk.
S225: The Regional Medical Director reviews clinical findings and approves changes to clinical guidance within the scope of regional authority.
S226: Audit findings identify the records examined, the criteria applied, and any limitations that affect interpretation.
S227: The Regional Dispatch Center retains audit evidence under approved access and retention controls.
S228: The Fleet Maintenance Cell uses the Mutual Aid Release Form to support accountable maintenance and availability records.
S229: Material findings are assigned to a responsible role with a due date and a documented method for verifying closure.
S230: The Shift Commander may restrict an operational capability when an unresolved defect creates unacceptable risk.
S231: The Regional Dispatch Center records the rationale, scope, and duration of each such restriction.
S232: Changes to the Ambulance Coordination Platform are assessed for operational, clinical, security, and continuity impacts before release.
S233: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console is tested against approved scenarios before a change is authorized for regional use.
S234: Release approval records identify the change owner, test evidence, known limitations, and rollback approach.
S235: The Radio Coordinator uses the South Access Lane Notice as part of accountable operational review.
S236: The Regional Radio Network and its interfaces are checked after maintenance or configuration changes before normal use resumes.
S237: Fleet Maintenance Cell schedules preventive work according to manufacturer guidance, service history, and regional operating requirements.
S238: Maintenance records include the asset identifier, work performed, parts used, and return-to-service decision.
S239: The Ambulance Coordination Platform is monitored for availability, response time, data integrity, and interface failures.
S240: The Regional Dispatch Center reviews service measures at a defined cadence and compares results with approved operating thresholds.
S241: Performance reviews consider demand, coverage, dispatch delay, communications availability, and unresolved data quality issues.
S242: The Hospital Liaison Desk contributes relevant operational observations while protecting information that is not required for the review.
S243: The Regional Medical Director and Shift Commander review significant events that may indicate a need for clinical or operational improvement.
S244: Corrective actions are tracked through verification so that completion is distinguished from demonstrated effectiveness.
S245: Recurring issues are evaluated for systemic causes rather than closed solely through local workarounds.
S246: Approved lessons are incorporated into procedures, training, maintenance plans, or release criteria as appropriate.
